audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never names a single Aatrox ability — it says 'W chain-pull', 'Q knockup chain', 'his passive heal', 'his R'. The packet flags this directly.
audit.why: Infernal Chains (W) is the ability that actually decides this lane: Nasus has no dash, so the pull is what converts a walk-up into a full Darkin Blade sequence. Naming it, and giving its real 825 range, turns vague advice into a positioning rule.
audit.corrected: Name Deathbringer Stance, The Darkin Blade, Infernal Chains, Umbral Dash and World Ender in early/mid/late/whys/spikes, and anchor the walk-up rule to Infernal Chains' 825 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere notes that Deathbringer Stance scales off the target's maximum health while Fury of the Sands grants Nasus bonus health.
audit.why: Riot's own text: Deathbringer Stance deals 'bonus magic damage and heals him, based on the target's max health'; Fury of the Sands 'gains increased Health ... and gains bonus Armor and Magic Resistance'. Popping R therefore raises the number his passive hits you for, and the bonus MR on the same ultimate is what offsets it. Nasus players who build raw HP against Aatrox are feeding the passive.
audit.corrected: Stated in notes for the user rather than forced into a fixed-length string; the R interaction is genuine but too long to land inside the length band on any existing field without displacing a higher-value fact.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. sequencingCues = 0. Not one 'wait for X before you Y' line exists in either layer.
audit.why: Infernal Chains is 20/18/16/14/12s — by far the longest non-ultimate cooldown Aatrox has, and it is the entry point to his combo against a dashless champion. The Darkin Blade is 14s at rank 1. Those two numbers define exactly when Nasus is allowed to step up and stack.
audit.corrected: Added explicit sequencing: do not walk into stacking range until Infernal Chains has missed; that buys 20s at rank 1. Added The Darkin Blade's 14s rank-1 cooldown to the cooldown breakdown.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early says 'Wither isn't up until 3'. The full layer's phases[1] says 'Wither online' at Level 2. The two layers contradict each other.
audit.why: Wither is a normal basic ability available from level 2 if it is taken there, which is the standard order into a hard-engage laner like Aatrox. The content layer's claim is wrong as stated and contradicts the sibling layer.
audit.corrected: Rewrote the closing clause of content.early so it no longer asserts a level for Wither, replacing it with the Infernal Chains cooldown window — higher value and not self-contradictory.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr and winCon both promise 'anti-heal', but the Itemization block lists Doran's Shield, Trinity Force, Iceborn Gauntlet, Frozen Heart, Plated Steelcaps and Sheen — no Grievous Wounds source at all.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal for this exact pairing (Deathbringer Stance, Umbral Dash, World Ender). World Ender explicitly grants 'increased healing', so the Grievous Wounds timing that matters is before his level-6 spike. The guide currently tells the player to anti-heal and then never tells them what to buy.
audit.corrected: Added Bramble Vest ahead of his level-6 World Ender to the Itemization line, replacing the redundant Sheen sentence already covered by the Trinity Force entry.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two Do/Don't entries have descriptions that do not match their titles: dosFull[2] 'Farm Q stacks safely' is described as 'Aatrox wastes World Ender — commit the full pattern immediately', and dontsFull[1] 'Fight before you have stacks' is described as 'Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown'.
audit.why: Both descriptions were clearly pasted from other slots. A player reading the card gets advice that contradicts the heading it sits under.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both descriptions to match their titles, using real numbers (Spirit Fire's flat 12s, Wither's 80 mana / 15s at rank 1).

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing notes that Spirit Fire's cooldown is flat 12s at every rank while its mana cost climbs 60 to 100.
audit.why: Players max E into ranged matchups expecting a faster shove. It never gets faster — only more expensive. In a lane where Nasus is forced to stack from range this changes how the level-3-to-5 mana budget is spent.
audit.corrected: Added the flat 12s fact to phases[2].why and to the dosFull entry about safe stacking.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash because we're both passive — he has no W chain-pull setup yet and I'm just soaking Siphoning Strike last-hits with Soul Eater lifesteal covering the chip. From level 2 it tilts to him fast: once his Q knockup chain and W are online he wins every extended trade and his passive heals back whatever I poke, so I do not contest the wave toe-to-toe. Eat the early CS, never stand in melee trading autos into his sweetspot Q, and just stack. Wither isn't up until 3, and even then it only peels a gank or punishes a hard overstep, not flips the lane.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash because we're both passive — Infernal Chains isn't online yet and I'm just soaking Siphoning Strike last-hits with Soul Eater lifesteal covering the chip. From level 2 it tilts to him fast: once The Darkin Blade and Infernal Chains are up he wins every extended trade and Umbral Dash's passive heal refunds whatever I poke, so I do not contest the wave toe-to-toe. Eat the early CS and never stand inside 825 units of a live Infernal Chains — that pull is what starts every combo on a champion with no dash. Once it misses I get 20 seconds to stack.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are his — I'm shoving or being chunked, hoarding stacks and playing not to die while his drain out-sustains anything I throw back. The danger is his W chain-pull into the full Q-Q-Q-R sequence; never get caught walking up where he can yank me into it. At 6 my Fury of the Sands lets me survive one committed all-in, but it does not win the duel outright against his R combat stats and heal — so I bait his R or chain-pull first, drop Wither on him mid-commit to gut his attack speed and kite, and live rather than greed the kill.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are his — I'm shoving or being chunked, hoarding stacks and playing not to die while Umbral Dash's drain out-sustains anything I throw back. The danger is Infernal Chains into the full Darkin Blade sequence; never get caught walking up while that pull is off cooldown. At 6 my Fury of the Sands lets me survive one committed all-in, but it does not beat World Ender's healing amp outright — so I make him spend Infernal Chains first, drop Wither on him mid-commit to gut his attack speed and kite, and live rather than greed the kill.

edits.before: This is where I take it back. By 2+ items my Q stacks one-shot through his HP, Spirit Fire's armor shred eats his durability, and Wither shuts off his R combat-stat all-in so his drain can't keep pace with my lifesteal and stacked damage. He spent the whole early game beating me but he can't out-scale a stacked Nasus the way a true-damage carry could — once I'm here a sustained fight is mine. So I survive his lane, refuse to int into his chain-pull combos before items, and cash the game out as a splitpush monster he simply can't duel anymore.
edits.after: This is where I take it back. By 2+ items my Q stacks one-shot through his HP, Spirit Fire's armor shred eats his durability, and Wither strips the Move Speed World Ender hands him so his drain can't keep pace with my lifesteal and stacked damage. He spent the whole early game beating me but he can't out-scale a stacked Nasus the way a true-damage carry could — once I'm here a sustained fight is mine so long as Grievous Wounds is on him. So I survive his lane, refuse to int into Infernal Chains before items, and cash out as a splitpush monster he can't duel.

notes: Deliberate omission: Aatrox's Umbral-Dash-during-The-Darkin-Blade repositioning (shifting the sweetspot mid-cast) is real high-elo tech and would be the single best addition to point 13, but animationCancels is null in aatrox.json and the brief forbids asserting it from the kit file. It is unverified here, not disproven — worth a wiki pass in a later run. Same for whether Wither's slow is reduced by tenacity (tenacityAffected is null for Nasus). Both halves are stated in Riot's text, so the composition is sound, but it needs a field with enough room to state it without dropping something better; every candidate string in this matchup was already at capacity.
